epidemic_simulation.note: Documented by name only; the sources record the tool function and no definition, and no primary paper was checked.

notation.meaning: an event: sender \(s_e\), receiver \(r_e\), time \(t_e\) (events are ordered; the history before time \(t\) is \(H_t\))
risk set at time \(t\): all ordered pairs \((s,r)\) of distinct actors
statistic vector of the dyad \((s,r)\) computed from \(H_t\)
weighted count of past events \(s\to r\) (with memory weights, below)

formulas.name: Ordinal relational event likelihood (Butts 2008; Perry and Wolfe 2013)
formulas.where: The partial likelihood of the observed order of events: at each event the observed dyad competes with every dyad of the risk set. Only the order of events enters, not the time gaps.

formulas.name: Score and Newton step
formulas.where: The log partial likelihood \(\ell=\log L\) is concave in \(\theta\); \(\mathbb E_{\theta,e}\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}_{\theta,e}\) are the mean and covariance of \(x\) over \(R_{t_e}\) with probabilities \(\propto e^{\theta^{\top}x}\). Standard errors are the square roots of the diagonal of \(\mathcal I(\hat\theta)^{-1}\). A finite maximizer exists only if the likelihood is not monotone.

variants.rem_fit: Coefficients and standard errors of the model above for a chosen statistic list; the statistics (and their memory) are those of rem_statistic. Which optimizer converges is not part of the definition.

edge_cases.definition_gives: With one event there is nothing to estimate from: the risk-set sums have a single factor and the likelihood is monotone.

remstats.behaviour: remify rejects a stream this short (one edge).

edge_cases.definition_gives: If the log partial likelihood is monotone in some direction (for example no event repeats a dyad when inertia is a statistic) the maximizer does not exist and no finite coefficient is defined.

remstats.behaviour: remstimate returns its last iterate; the definition has no finite estimate (reference value reported as -999).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Where a maximizer exists it is unique (the log likelihood is concave), so differences are due to the optimizer, not the definition.

remstats.behaviour: remstimate's coefficients differ by up to a few percent on complete5_dir and gnp_dir_dense, while the reference agrees with an independent Newton iteration to 1e-11 there; the difference is in remstimate's optimizer.

rem_statistic.note: Recency statistics (rank-based) and the event-type and weighted variants are named in the sources but their formulas are not written here. The count definitions follow the statistic names of the remstats manual; the original paper formulas were not checked for every statistic.

notation.meaning: an event: sender \(s_e\), receiver \(r_e\), time \(t_e\) (events are ordered; the history before time \(t\) is \(H_t\))
risk set at time \(t\): all ordered pairs \((s,r)\) of distinct actors
statistic vector of the dyad \((s,r)\) computed from \(H_t\)
weighted count of past events \(s\to r\) (with memory weights, below)

formulas.name: Memory weights (Butts 2008; Brandes et al. 2009)
formulas.where: Past events count fully, only inside a window of width \(T\), or with an exponential weight of half-life \(T\) (the factor \(\ln2/T\) is that of Brandes et al. 2009; other tools may omit it).

formulas.name: Dyad statistics from counts (Butts 2008; Perry and Wolfe 2013; Arena et al. 2026)
formulas.latex: \begin{aligned}\text{inertia}&=c_{sr},&\text{reciprocity}&=c_{rs},\\ \text{outdegree sender}&=\sum_h c_{sh},&\text{indegree sender}&=\sum_h c_{hs},\\ \text{outdegree receiver}&=\sum_h c_{rh},&\text{indegree receiver}&=\sum_h c_{hr}\end{aligned}
formulas.where: Counts of past events involving the sender and receiver of the dyad, over \(h\ne\) the dyad's own actors as stated by each tool; computed at time \(t\) from the history only.

formulas.name: Triadic statistics
formulas.where: Two-path (outgoing/incoming) and shared-partner statistics; \(\phi\) combines the two counts of a partner: the minimum, the product, or an indicator that both are positive.

variants.rem_statistic: One statistic per call: the dyad statistic of every event's own dyad and its sum over the risk set; the memory weights \(g\) and the combination \(\phi\) change the value. remstats: the first event has an empty history.

edge_cases.definition_gives: No events: there is no history and no statistic row.
Not in the risk set \(R_t\) (distinct actors only); loops in the data are dropped before counting.
With one event the history before it is empty and every count is 0 by the formula.

remstats.behaviour: remify rejects a stream this short (one edge).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Event weights are not part of the count formulas above; counting weighted events is a different definition.

notation.meaning: a contact: an edge from source \(u\) to target \(v\) (or between \(u\) and \(v\) if undirected) active at time \(t\)
start and end of the observation window; only contacts with \(t_0\le t\le t_1\) are used
earliest arrival time at \(v\) over time-respecting paths from \(s\); \(\infty\) if there is none

formulas.name: Time-respecting path and earliest arrival (Kempe et al. 2002; Holme and Saramaki 2012)
formulas.latex: A(s,v)=\min\Bigl\{t_k:\ (s{=}v_0,v_1,t_1),\dots,(v_{k-1},v_k{=}v,t_k)\text{ contacts},\ t_0\le t_1\le\dots\le t_k\le t_1^{\mathrm{end}}\Bigr\},\qquad A(s,s)=t_0
formulas.where: A path may wait at a node and may use several contacts with the same time (traversal time 0, non-strict ordering \(t_i\le t_{i+1}\)). \(t_1^{\mathrm{end}}\) is the end of the window. Unreachable nodes have \(A=\infty\). Strict ordering \(t_i<t_{i+1}\) would give a different value on simultaneous contacts.

variants.temporal_paths: Earliest-arrival time from a source to every node (as arrival time, i.e. the start plus the elapsed time); other criteria (latest departure, fastest, shortest) change the minimized quantity and are not covered.

edge_cases.definition_gives: \(A(s,s)=t_0\) and no other node exists.

tsna.behaviour: No difference from the reference value recorded on the compared inputs of this kind (single_node).

edge_cases.definition_gives: No contacts: \(A(s,v)=\infty\) for every \(v\ne s\).

tsna.behaviour: No difference from the reference value recorded on the compared inputs of this kind (empty).

edge_cases.definition_gives: A node without contacts is never reached: \(A=\infty\).

tsna.behaviour: No difference from the reference value recorded on the compared inputs of this kind (empty, single_node, two_triangles_isolate, gnp_und_sparse).

edge_cases.definition_gives: If no time-respecting path along source to target exists, \(A=\infty\); reachability is not symmetric.

tsna.behaviour: No difference from the reference value recorded on the compared inputs of this kind (gnp_dir_sparse, weighted_dir, multi_loops_dir).

edge_cases.definition_gives: For undirected contacts both orientations are usable; for directed contacts only source to target.

tsna.behaviour: No difference from the reference value recorded on the compared inputs of this kind (karate, gnp_dir_dense).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Contacts with equal times can be chained when the ordering is non-strict, as in the formula above.

tsna.behaviour: No difference from the reference value recorded on the compared inputs of this kind (karate, kite, les_miserables).

edge_cases.definition_gives: Repeated contacts only add candidate times; the minimum in \(A\) is unchanged by duplicates of the same time.

tsna.behaviour: No difference from the reference value recorded on the compared inputs of this kind (multi_loops_und, multi_loops_dir).

formulas.name: Forward reachable set size
formulas.where: The number of other nodes reachable from \(s\) by a time-respecting path in the window; subtracting the source removes the trivial path to itself.

variants.temporal_reach: Count of nodes with finite earliest arrival time from the source, excluding the source.
